title: Centre for Experience Economy and Cities - Home
gist: Promotional landing page for the World Economic Forum's Centre for Experience Economy and Cities, arguing that local conditions drive most business costs and supply chain disruptions. It cites engagement with 130+ cities and 185+ business partners and highlights a Mexico City open-data case linked to a >50% cut in high-impact crime.

themes.theme: Localization of business costs and supply chain risk

insights.claim: According to the World Economic Forum's Centre for Experience Economy and Cities, over 70% of business operating costs are shaped by local conditions.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
entities: Centre for Experience Economy and Cities
insights.so_what: If most costs are local, site selection and city-level policy are material drivers of corporate margins, not just macro factors.
insights.quote: Over 70% of business operating costs are shaped by local conditions
insights.locator: We advance global progress through local action

insights.claim: The World Economic Forum states that 80% of supply chain disruptions originate regionally, which it argues makes place-based collaboration critical for global resilience and competitiveness.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Supply chain risk analysis should weight regional/local exposures heavily when assessing operational resilience.
insights.quote: 80% of supply chain disruptions originate regionally—underscoring the critical role of place-based collaboration for global resilience and competitiveness.
insights.locator: We advance global progress through local action

themes.theme: WEF cities programme scope and focus areas

insights.claim: The World Economic Forum's Centre for Experience Economy and Cities reports engaging 130+ cities, 185+ business partners and 60+ civil society collaborators.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
entities: Centre for Experience Economy and Cities
insights.so_what: Indicates the breadth of the public-private network shaping city-level policy agendas that companies may engage with.

insights.claim: The WEF Centre for Experience Economy and Cities organizes its work around three initiatives: infrastructure and built environment, innovation ecosystems, and the experience economy.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
entities: Centre for Experience Economy and Cities
insights.so_what: Flags city infrastructure, urban innovation and experience/visitor economies as themes the WEF is pushing with public and private partners.
insights.locator: Transforming how we live, work and play

themes.theme: Case studies: open data and urban deliveries

insights.claim: The World Economic Forum says it supported Mexico City in updating its open data policy, which helped the city reduce high-impact crime by more than 50% as part of a comprehensive crime-reduction strategy.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: A claimed large public-safety improvement in a major emerging-market city, though attribution to open data within a broader strategy is unquantified.
insights.quote: helped the city reduce high-impact crime by more than 50% as part of a comprehensive crime-reduction strategy

insights.claim: The World Economic Forum convened leading delivery companies to advance joint commitments for collaborating with cities and transforming the urban deliveries ecosystem.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Signals coordinated industry-city engagement on last-mile delivery that could shape future urban logistics regulation.
insights.locator: How companies are creating a more sustainable future
